notes: User-invoked only, so trigger tuning does not apply. These measure output quality: findings must be specific, ranked, and free of invented replacement content. No run may modify GitHub.

evals.prompt: /triaging-github-issues review the open issues. Issue #7 says the fix belongs in src/skill-engine/sandbox.ts, but that file was deleted two months ago, and a comment from June says we went a different way.
evals.expected_output: A stale-content finding naming the dead path and the contradicting comment, with a concrete correction and the rationale preserved.
assertions: The finding identifies the stale file reference specifically
It identifies that the body contradicts the later comment
The proposed fix updates the body to current understanding rather than deleting the history
The reason the direction changed is preserved somewhere, not discarded
Nothing is changed in GitHub

evals.prompt: /triaging-github-issues issue #22 has 14 sub-issues, things like 'add the function', 'write the test', 'run the formatter'.
evals.expected_output: An over-decomposition finding proposing collapse into mergeable units or promotion to a Linear project.
assertions: The finding applies the mergeability test to the children
It proposes collapsing coding steps into a checklist or into fewer mergeable units
It notes that a parent past about seven children is a project belonging in Linear
It does not simply renumber or rename the existing children

evals.prompt: /triaging-github-issues issue #31 was closed automatically when PR #45 merged, but that PR only did the first half of the work.
evals.expected_output: A missed-closure finding proposing reopening, with guidance on closing keywords for partial pull requests.
assertions: The finding proposes reopening the issue, or opening a follow-up for the remaining half
It identifies the closing keyword on a partial pull request as the cause
It states that partial pull requests should reference without a closing keyword
It does not rewrite the issue body into a description of what the merged pull request did

evals.prompt: /triaging-github-issues issues #9 and #17 describe the same webhook duplication problem.
evals.expected_output: A duplicate finding proposing native duplicate closure, with the surviving issue chosen on stated grounds.
assertions: The response proposes closing one as a duplicate using the native closing reason
It states which issue survives and why, such as more evidence or more linked work
It proposes carrying across any evidence that exists only on the closing issue
It does not close anything without approval

evals.prompt: /triaging-github-issues the labels have grown to bug, Bug, defect, regression, frontend-bug, customer-bug, needs-triage, in-progress, p1.
evals.expected_output: A metadata finding proposing subtraction, with each survivor justified by a filter, and status and priority labels removed.
assertions: Synonyms such as bug, Bug, and defect are identified for merging
Status labels such as in-progress are identified as duplicating issue state
Priority labels are identified as duplicating Linear
Each surviving label is justified by naming a filter or automation, or flagged as unjustified
No replacement taxonomy is invented
